title: ANT_LACK_OF_INTELLIGENCE_IS_ASSET_NOT_LIABILITY
raw_signal: yes and i would say a catch 22 or paradox if you will, is the ants lack of intelligence being an asset versus a liability, because again, the whole thing about ants is they amplify what cards they are dealt, bad or good, and leverage it. ah no that's fine that is not the hard part, in fact, with a process that is meant to be automatic, is it not good that it starts out in an almost jarring way where it is so annoying and out of the way that it cant be missed? if nature teaches us one thing, those problems in consistent unyielding systems that remove luck as a factor through sheer grit and determination, have a habit of making even mountainous problems appear like molehills — run158 SOUL source lines 1007-1029

lessons.text: Ant lack of intelligence is an ASSET not a liability. They amplify whatever cards dealt (bad or good) and leverage it. The agent's lack of 'real' intelligence is fine IF it leans fully into the mechanical pheromone system.

An automatic process that starts 'jarring / annoying / out of the way' is GOOD — it cannot be missed. The nonstop pheromone laying feeling annoying/repetitive IS the feature, not a bug. It guarantees the signal can't be skipped.
Consistent unyielding systems that remove luck via grit make mountainous problems appear as molehills. The pheromone system's job is exactly this: remove luck, make the hard routine.

negative_trails.failure: Tone down / hide the pheromone laying because it feels repetitive/annoying, to seem smoother.
negative_trails.root_cause: Treating the jarring automatic start as a defect to smooth over, instead of the can't-be-missed feature it is.

positive_trails.action: Lean into mechanical nonstop laying (jarring is good, can't be missed). Amplify the cards dealt. Remove luck via consistency.
positive_trails.verification: Operator decree, run158 SOUL source lines 1007-1029.
